info.title: ManyPI API
info.description: The REST API behind ManyPI — AI lead generation, email validation, cold-email outreach, agent runs and web scraping. Every endpoint is authenticated with a ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) or an OAuth 2.1 access token, and honours the permissions granted to that credential.

tags.name: Leads
tags.description: Find, store, enrich and manage leads.

tags.name: Email validation
tags.description: Verify that lead addresses can receive mail.

tags.name: Outreach
tags.description: Inboxes, sequences, campaigns, sending and replies.

tags.name: Endpoints
tags.description: Publish scrapers as typed REST endpoints.

get.description:
List and filter the workspace's leads. Also returns the declared custom columns, the past lead searches that produced these leads, the workspace total and the plan's lead limit — everything a grid needs in one call.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free text across company, full name, email and domain.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: A lead status, or `archived` / `unsubscribed` (which are flags, not statuses).

parameters.name: campaign
parameters.description: The agent run id of the lead search that produced the leads.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: Narrow to one brand, or `all` for the whole workspace.

workspaceTotal.description: Every lead the workspace stores, ignoring filters.

campaigns.description: Past lead searches, with how many leads each produced.

patch.description:
Change status and/or archive state for up to 500 leads at once.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Permanently delete up to 500 leads. Consider archiving instead — archived leads stop appearing everywhere but stay recoverable.

Requires the `write` permission.

patch.description:
Update one field, the status, the score, or the archive flag on a single lead. Setting `field` to a name that is not a core field writes into the lead's custom columns.

Requires the `write` permission.

field.description: A core field (`company`, `full_name`, `title`, `email`, `phone`, `domain`, `linkedin_url`, `location`, `source_url`) or a custom column key.

value.description: Empty string or null clears the field.

delete.description:
Permanently delete one lead.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Launch the lead-generation agent against structured criteria, a saved search, or a set of seed leads ("find more like these").

The run is asynchronous: poll `GET /api/agents/runs` with the returned `conversation_id`. The run may pause with a clarifying question — answer it with `POST /api/agents/runs/{id}/reply` and the same run continues.

`count` is clamped to the workspace's remaining lead capacity; when that happens the response carries a `clamped` block. A full workspace returns `403` with `code: "lead_limit"`.

Requires the `agents` permission.

profile_id.description: Re-run a saved search. Its criteria are used unless `criteria` overrides them.

seed_lead_ids.description: Seed the search from existing leads ("find similar").

save.description: Persist as a reusable saved search.

criteria.description: E-commerce agencies building Shopify stores for DTC brands

count.description: Leads the run will actually try to save, after clamping.

clamped.description: Present only when `count` was reduced to fit the plan.

403.description: The workspace is storing all the leads the plan allows (`code: "lead_limit"`).

get.description:
The workspace's saved lead searches, plus past lead-generation campaigns that were never saved as a profile.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.summary: Create or update a saved search
post.description:
Store a search without running it. Pass `id` to update an existing profile in place.

Requires the `write` permission.

Write a batch of leads. **Up to 100 rows per request** — chunk larger files client-side so a big import cannot outlive the request timeout and so progress is real.

`declare_fields` lets the same request that carries the first chunk also declare the custom columns those rows write into. It is idempotent, so resending the declarations with every chunk is harmless.

A full workspace still returns `200` — the rows that fitted were written — with `code: "lead_limit"` in the body.

Requires the `write` permission.

duplicates.description: `merge` fills blanks on the existing lead; `overwrite` lets incoming values win; `skip` leaves it untouched.

skippedNoIdentity.description: No email and no domain-plus-name, so there is nothing to file the row under.

remaining.description: Lead slots left after this batch.

code.description: `lead_limit` when the plan filled up mid-import.

get.description:
Stream the filtered leads as CSV, up to 10,000 rows. Honours the same `status` and `q` filters as the list endpoint. Archived leads are excluded unless you ask for them.

Requires the `read` permission.

How many more leads the workspace can store. Read this before starting a large search or import — it changes every time a run saves a lead.

Requires the `read` permission.

The workspace's declared lead columns, in display order. These are column *definitions*; the values live on each lead's `custom` object.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Declare a column so leads can carry it. Set `auto_research` and the agent fills it in on future lead searches without you restating it each time.

Requires the `write` permission.

200.description: The column already existed and was returned unchanged.

post.description:
Queue an SMTP mailbox probe for lead addresses, raw addresses, or both. Results are written back onto the leads as `email_status`, `email_provider`, `email_is_role` and `email_validated_at`.

Pass `estimate_only` to price the run without queueing it. You are only charged for probes that actually run — cached results and addresses rejected by the cheap pre-check are free.

Requires the `leads:validate` permission, deliberately separate from `write` so a general-purpose key cannot run up a validation bill.

lead_ids.description: Leads in this workspace whose addresses should be checked.

emails.description: Raw addresses, not tied to a lead.

estimate_only.description: Price the run without queueing it.

200.description: The job was queued, or (with `estimate_only`) priced.

402.description: Out of validation credits and overage is off (`code: "validation_credits_exhausted"`).

get.description:
The workspace's recent validation jobs, newest first.

Requires the `read` permission.

One validation job plus its per-address results. Poll this for progress and the final breakdown.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: items
parameters.description: Set to `false` to omit the per-address results.

get.description:
Every connected sending identity with its health: today's sends versus the warmup-aware cap, 14-day delivered/failed/opened/bounced, a rolling 24-hour bounce rate, whether the bounce guard has paused it, and a 0–100 health score.

Use an inbox `id` as `smtp_config_id` when creating a campaign or sending.

Requires the `read` permission.

parameters.name: brand
parameters.description: `all` reports every inbox in the workspace.

get.description:
Saved email sequences with their inline steps. Brand-scoped; `?brand=all` widens to the whole workspace.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Create the email steps a campaign sends. Step 0 goes out on enrollment; each later step waits `wait_days` after the previous one and, with `thread_mode: "reply"`, threads under the first email. Merge variables: `{{first_name}}`, `{{company}}`, `{{title}}`, `{{domain}}`, `{{location}}`. Bodies are simple HTML — `

`, `
`, ``, ``. A/B variants inside a step require Pro or Business. Requires the `write` permission.

403.description: A/B variants require Pro or Business.

post.description:
AI-draft a cold email (`mode: "email"`) or a whole follow-up sequence (`mode: "sequence"`) from a plain-language brief, written against your brand context.

This only drafts: nothing is saved and nothing is sent. Feed the result into `POST /api/outreach/sequences` or `POST /api/outreach/send`.

Requires the `read` permission.

lead_id.description: An example lead to tailor the tone toward.

example.instructions: We help e-commerce agencies find new client leads without cold-calling. Ask for a 15-minute call.

get.description:
Campaigns with per-campaign stats — enrolled, active, completed, sent, opened, replied — plus the sequence and inbox each is bound to.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Bind a sequence to a sending inbox. After creating it, enroll leads with `POST /api/outreach/enroll`.

Requires the `write` permission.

daily_limit.description: Never exceeds the inbox's own cap.

priority.description: Higher wins the next paced slot when campaigns share an inbox.

patch.description:
Pause, resume or archive a campaign, or change its name, reply-to, daily limit, schedule or priority. Pausing stops further sends without losing progress.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a campaign. Archiving (`PATCH` with `status: "archived"`) is usually the better choice — it keeps the history.

Requires the `write` permission.

get.description:
One campaign's full analytics: headline stats, a per-step sent/opened breakdown, and every enrolled lead with its progress.

The per-step breakdown is where you see whether the follow-ups are doing the work.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Queue the campaign's sequence for real sending, respecting the inbox's warmup and daily caps. Up to 1,000 leads per call.

Skipped rather than failed: leads with no email, leads already enrolled, suppressed or unsubscribed addresses, and addresses known to be undeliverable. When the brand has *validate on enroll* turned on (the default), unchecked addresses are validated first and undeliverable ones dropped before anything is sent.

**Sending cannot be undone.** Requires a paid plan and the `outreach:send` permission.

403.description: Outreach requires a paid plan (`code: "outreach_locked"`), or the workspace is over its seat count.

delete.description:
Cancel remaining steps for the given leads. Emails already sent cannot be recalled.

Requires the `outreach:send` permission.

post.description:
Send a single email to a lead now, outside any sequence. Merge variables are rendered against the lead, the inbox's daily/warmup cap is respected, and the lead is marked `contacted`.

**Cannot be undone.** Requires a paid plan and the `outreach:send` permission.

lead_id.description: Used for merge variables and as the default recipient.

to.description: Explicit recipient; defaults to the lead's address.

get.description:
Workspace-wide sending activity: 14 days of sends (sent, failed, opened per day), replies per day, unsubscribes, bounces, active enrollments, and today's sent versus the combined warmup-aware cap.

Requires the `read` permission.

bounced.description: Bucketed by send date, not bounce date, so the figure lines up with the batch that caused it.

unsubRate14d.description: Percentage rounded to a whole number: `4` means 4%.

bounceRate14d.description: Percentage to one decimal place: `9.2` means 9.2%.

sent24h.description: Sends in the last rolling 24 hours, which is the window `capToday` applies to.

capToday.description: Warmup-aware caps summed across every connected inbox.

get.description:
Everything that came back from your campaigns — human replies, auto-replies and bounces — with counts for filter chips and a sentiment summary.

Reading replies requires any paid plan. The **sentiment fields** (`sentiment`, `sentiment_score`, `intent`, `summary`, `analyzed_at`) require Pro or Business and are stripped from the response on other plans.

Requires the `read` permission.

Patterns across your replies and concrete, approvable suggestions for what to change.

Requires Pro or Business, and the `read` permission.

403.description: Reply intelligence requires Pro or Business.

get.description:
The workspace's do-not-contact list. Nothing on it is ever sent to, by any campaign, from any inbox, in any brand.

Pass `format=csv` to download the whole list.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Add addresses to the do-not-contact list. Import your existing list on day one — customers, competitors, anyone who has already asked you to stop.

Requires the `write` permission.

delete.description:
Remove one address from the list. This only clears the block — it does not re-enroll anyone, so a mistaken removal cannot by itself restart emails to someone who opted out.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Start an agent run on a natural-language goal. Asynchronous — poll `GET /api/agents/runs/{id}` for status and results.

A run that hits an ambiguity **pauses** and asks a question rather than guessing; read it from `result_summary` and answer with `POST /api/agents/runs/{id}/reply` to resume the same run.

Requires the `agents` permission.

goal.description: What you want ManyPI to do, in plain language.

output_schema.description: A JSON schema the result must conform to.

example.goal: Find the pricing pages of the ten largest Shopify agencies in Berlin and summarise their packages.

403.description: Too many runs already in flight for the plan.

get.description:
Your recent runs, newest first, narrowed to the workspace and brand you are working in.

Requires the `read` permission.

Full status for one run, plus its artifacts with signed download URLs valid for one hour.

When `status` is `paused`, the agent's question is in `result_summary`.

Requires the `read` permission.

delete.description:
Delete a run along with its events and artifacts.

Requires the `write` permission.

post.description:
Deliver a message into a run.

- **Paused run** — the reply is submitted as the answer to the agent's pending question and the *same* run continues mid-thought.
- **Finished run** (`completed` / `failed` / `cancelled`) — a follow-up run starts in the same conversation, inheriting its context and playbook, so "find 25 more like those" keeps saving leads.
- **Still working** — `409`, unless you pass `interrupt: true`, which cancels it and starts a new run with your message.

Requires the `agents` permission.

interrupt.description: Stop a still-working run, then start a new one with this message.

example.message: Only agencies with a team page and at least five people.

409.description: The run is still working. Wait for it to pause or finish, cancel it, or pass `interrupt: true`.

post.description:
Stop a run immediately. Cancellation is authoritative rather than advisory — the run is marked cancelled at once, so a wedged executor cannot keep it "running" and occupying one of your parallel-run slots.

Requires the `agents` permission.

get.description:
Skills available to the caller: ManyPI's premade ones plus the workspace's own.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Create a custom skill — a reusable instruction set injected into the agent's system prompt for a run.

Instructions shape behaviour but never widen tool access: custom skills are always created with the safe defaults.

Requires the `write` permission.

example.title: Company research
example.system_prompt: For the company given, research what they sell, who their customers are, recent funding or hiring news, and the two people most likely to own the buying decision. Cite a source URL for every fact.

get.description:
The workspace's scrapers with their schema, target URL, status and type.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Queue a scraper run. **Asynchronous** — the call returns `202` immediately with a `runId`, so a slow page never times your request out.

Read the result with `GET /api/{scraperId}/data/{runId}`, or configure an outbound webhook to be notified when it completes.

Requires the `scraper` permission.

parameters.name: scraperId
parameters.description: Find this in the dashboard under Scrapers.

url.description: Override the scraper's saved target for this run.

404.description: No such scraper for this account.

get.description:
The status and extracted data for one run. Poll this after `POST /api/scrape/{scraperId}` until `status` is `completed`.

Requires the `read` permission.

Recent scraper runs across every scraper, with status and extracted data. Returned as a flat array, which is the shape polling-based integrations such as Zapier expect for a trigger.

Requires the `read` permission.

Your published endpoints and the scrapers backing them.

Requires the `read` permission.

post.description:
Publish a scraper as a typed REST endpoint at `https://app.manypi.com/v1/e/{slug}`.

Slugs are unique per account and resolve within the key owner's endpoints, so your slug namespace is your own.

Requires the `write` permission.

param_schema.description: JSON Schema for the input. Validated on every call.

403.description: Endpoint limit reached for the plan.

409.description: That slug is already in use.

get.description:
Call one of your published endpoints.

How a call resolves: a fresh cached result is returned immediately (no crawl credits spent); otherwise the scrape runs inline, up to a ~110 second budget; if it exceeds that — or the endpoint is `async` — you get `202` with a run id to poll at `GET /v1/e/{slug}/results/{runId}`.

Requires the `endpoints:invoke` permission.

200.description: The extracted data, matching the endpoint's output schema.

400.description: Parameters failed validation against the endpoint's schema.

404.description: No endpoint with that slug for this account.

get.summary: Validate a key / get account info
get.description: The cheapest way to confirm a key works. Returns the owning user, the key's permissions and its rate limit.

bearerAuth.description: A ManyPI API key (`mpi_...`) from Settings → API keys, or an OAuth 2.1 access token obtained through the MCP consent flow.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, invalid or expired credential — or a key that lacks the permission this route requires.

BadRequest.description: The request body or parameters failed validation.

NotFound.description: No such resource in this workspace.

code.description: A machine-readable code on gated failures: `lead_limit`, `outreach_locked`, `validation_credits_exhausted`.

custom.description: Values for the workspace's declared custom columns.

agent_run_id.description: The lead search that produced this lead.

auto_research.description: The agent fills this in on future lead searches.

key.description: Derived from the label when absent.

ImportRow.description: A lead needs an email, or a domain plus a name, or it cannot be filed and is skipped.

custom.description: Keys must match declared columns, or the values are dropped.

LeadResearchCriteria.description: The structured search. The description does most of the work; the rest is what the agent enforces.

count.description: How many NEW leads to save. Clamped to remaining plan capacity.

company_size.description: Free text on purpose: "5-50 employees", "Series A", "under $5M ARR".

titles.description: Roles to reach inside each company.

exclusions.description: Hard excludes — matches are dropped, not saved.

required_fields.description: A lead missing one of these is not saved.

extra_columns.description: Extra researched columns, written to the lead's custom fields.

sources.description: Where to look: directories, marketplaces, maps, specific sites.

counts.description: How many addresses landed in each status.

name.description: The inbox label, which is often the address itself.

from.description: The sending address. Falls back to the SMTP username when no from-address is set.

sent24h.description: Sends in the last rolling 24 hours — the window `cap` applies to.

cap.description: Warmup-aware cap for the current window, not the raw daily limit.

dailyLimit.description: The inbox's configured daily limit, before warmup is applied.

bounceRate14d.description: Percentage to one decimal place: `9.2` means 9.2%.

warmingUp.description: True while the inbox is still ramping and `cap` is below `dailyLimit`.

sendingPausedAt.description: Set when the bounce guard paused the inbox.

health.description: Delivery success rate, capped at 94 while warming up and reduced four points per percent of 14-day bounce rate.

subject.description: Merge variables allowed. Empty on a `reply` step, which sends as "Re:" the first email's subject.

wait_days.description: Days after the previous step. Step 0 is 0.

send_days.description: Weekdays to send on, as `Date.getDay()` numbers: 0 is Sunday, 1 is Monday, 6 is Saturday. Values outside 0-6 are discarded, so an ISO-style Sunday of 7 is dropped rather than honoured. Defaults to `[1,2,3,4,5]` when omitted, or when every supplied value is discarded.

inbox_strategy.description: How sends are spread when several inboxes are available.

include_unsubscribe.description: Whether an unsubscribe link is appended to each email.

require_verified.description: Whether unverified addresses are validated before enrollment.

unsubscribed_sends.description: Sends that went to an address which later opted out.

sentiment.description: Pro and Business only; stripped from the response on other plans.

result_summary.description: The result — or, while `paused`, the agent's question to you.

download_url.description: Signed URL, valid for one hour.

scraper_schema.description: The JSON Schema the extracted data conforms to.

result.description: Present once the run is completed.
